title: Osero inherits Total Risk Capital requirements as a base class, and changes to that base propagate into the Osero Artifact automatically
content:
A.6.1.1.7.2.6.1.2.1.3.2 states that as operators of the Osero Liquidity Layer, "Stablewatch automatically inherits, and is subject to, the base class of operational requirements related to Total Risk Capital management defined in A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2 - Primes' Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management. Modifications to the base operational logic automatically propagate to the Osero Artifact."

The language is explicitly object-oriented, and the second sentence is the consequential one. Risk requirements are not copied into the Artifact at a point in time; they are inherited live. When the ecosystem tightens the base class, Osero's obligations tighten immediately.

The upside is uniformity that cannot decay. Without inheritance, every Prime would hold its own snapshot of risk rules and an ecosystem-wide tightening would require a separate governance action in each Agent — with the Agents most in need of tightening being the most likely to resist. Inheritance removes the negotiation.

The tension with Osero's own governance is real and worth naming. A.6.1.1.7.2.2.2.2.1.2.1 gives OSERO token holders a Root Edit process for amending the Artifact, and A.6.1.1.7.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.6 forbids edits that violate the Atlas. Here a portion of the Artifact's content changes with no proposal, no Facilitator review, and no vote. Token holders hold amendment rights over the Artifact's own text but not over the parts that flow in by reference.

The practical implication for anyone reading the Artifact: it is not self-contained. Determining Osero's actual risk obligations requires reading A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2 as it stands today, not the Osero Artifact as last amended.
